about: Published context measurements. Speed aggregations identify their source files and sample counts. Disk figures are payload calculations and hypothetical transfer lower bounds, not measured model speeds.
setup: Qwen3.8-27B with FP8 weights and a 16-bit attention cache, two Intel Arc Pro B70 GPUs, R314 runtime, one request at a time.

window.cold_method: Initial bare-text probe, cache off, one request at each length. Input speeds and latency only; follow-up chat probes repaired answer-format and output-limit problems.

cache.state_memory: the memory of about 2,500 tokens of context

comparison.task: A stream of 20 batches (121,000 tokens) of counter updates with overwrites and deletes. A delivered batch cannot be fetched again. At the end: the current value of 24 counters.
comparison.seeds: Seed 0 for the original arms; seeds 0 and 1 for revised self-editing.

rows.strategy: Large window, exact cache on
rows.note: First seed: the model filtered batches with code and about 91% of prompt tokens were cached. Second seed: no answers. It let every batch into its context and re-typed it, grew about 13K tokens per batch, and the server refused the next request at about 246K, one batch before the questions arrived. Its running table was exact up to that point; it had never been told its window size.

trials.note: Filtered batches with code; every final answer correct.
Context filled before the final questions arrived; no answers returned.

rows.strategy: Original self-editing agent
rows.note: all 5 losses were batches its own rollback-and-retry removed after delivery

rows.strategy: Summarise at 75% of the budget
rows.note: 12 summaries, 57 calls; rewritten history reduces prefix reuse.

rows.strategy: Self-editing, files allowed
rows.note: no edit was needed

rows.strategy: No management, files allowed
Large window, earlier reasoning removed
rows.note: stuck re-deriving its state every call; never acted

rows.strategy: Improved self-editing agent
rows.note: No delivered batch was lost. The first seed was fully right. On the second, 3 of 24 were wrong: the model re-typed its own batch-folding script with a mistake, so deletes stopped being applied from batch 17 on. A harness check on each fold is being tested.

trials.note: No delivered batch lost; all final values correct.
All batches retained. A re-typed fold script stopped applying deletes from batch 17, causing three wrong final values.

rows.strategy: Improved self-editing agent, thinking only when needed
rows.note: The fold script is written once and checked by the harness on every batch; thinking is on only at the start, after an error and for the final answer. Right on both seeds, including the one where the earlier version dropped its delete rule.

rows.strategy: Improved self-editing agent, 480K stream (larger than the window)
rows.note: 478K tokens in 76 batches, 1.8 times the whole window. The model wrote one small script, kept its table in the pinned state and piped each batch through the script; it read only 2 of the 76 batches itself. Shows unlimited input when code can do the reading, not yet the model understanding more text than its window.

rows.strategy: Files allowed, 480K stream
rows.note: The same 478K stream with files allowed: no management (11 calls) and self-editing (12 calls). Both saved the batches to disk and computed the answers with a script.

rows.strategy: Improved self-editing agent, prose ledger (the model must read)
rows.note: Different task: the same counters, but every batch is narrative text that a short script cannot parse (an 80-line parser scores 13-33%). Not a valid reading test: the agent's instructions told it to write a fold script, so it spent the run building a parser instead of reading. It fetched 6 of 20 batches in 120 calls and also broke the no-files rule. A calibrated narrative task was built afterwards; see the rows below.

rows.strategy: Read-mode self-editing agent, narrative text (the model must read)
rows.note: Different task: 119K of ordinary narrative with three real counter changes per 2K batch, numbers written as words, calibrated so that a single step is about 98% right. With guards on the agent loop (no repeated command, no state change without a batch in view, no silent dropped lines): seed 0 got 23 of 24 (one reading slip, one dropped counter); seed 1 asks 18 counters and got all 18, with its table matching the hidden reference after every batch, but is void by the letter of the no-files rule because it wrote the whole table into the answers file before the questions arrived. Before the guards seed 0 was 20 of 24 in 10 minutes.

rows.strategy: Keep everything in the window, narrative text
rows.note: Same narrative task. Everything stayed in view and the model read it all at the end with thinking on. 120K fits the window; a 480K stream would not.

rows.strategy: No management, files allowed, narrative text
rows.note: Same narrative task. The model saved the batches to files, wrote a script that pulls out the sentences naming a counter, and read only those. Search narrowed the reading; nothing was lost because the text stayed on disk.

rows.strategy: Read-mode self-editing agent, narrative text, 480K stream (larger than the window)
rows.note: 479,512 tokens of narrative in 240 batches, 1.8 times the whole window, read at a 32K budget with the guarded agent: 634 calls, 576 with thinking off, 287 edits of its own context, no rule broken, no parser. The model read more than it can hold, by understanding, and kept an exact running table. One seed; the second is queued. The same agent without the guards had failed on this stream.

rows.strategy: Table plus archive and recall, narrative text with questions about dropped text
rows.note: Retention test: the 119K narrative task plus twelve questions, asked only at the end, about values later overwritten and incidental details. Dropped batches go verbatim to an archive the model can only read, with a search tool. Every answer right, including the twelve about dropped text; it searched the archive 12 times. Nothing is deleted, only moved out of view.

rows.strategy: Table only (read-mode agent), same retention test
rows.note: A running table cannot answer questions about the past, as designed: 6 blank, 5 wrong.

rows.strategy: Summarise at 75%, same retention test
rows.note: Summarising also got everything right: with thinking on, its eight summaries kept the old values. Four times slower than the archive agent and eight times the writing.

rows.strategy: Keep everything in the window, same retention test
rows.note: Two wrong with the whole text in view.

rows.strategy: No management, files allowed, same retention test
rows.note: The plain agent thought its way through its 32K budget in 25 calls before it had finished reading, and the budget stop ended it. The same agent got 24 of 24 on the version without the extra questions; it has no guards and its results swing.

rows.strategy: Paper's self-editing agent (as released, lab harness fixes only), narrative text
rows.note: Same 119K narrative task. Right, but seven times slower than the guarded read-mode agent: the difference is thinking tokens.

rows.strategy: Summarise at 75%, narrative text
rows.note: Same 119K narrative task; seven summaries.

rows.strategy: Guarded read-mode agent, 6 changes per batch
rows.note: Twice the reading density of the calibrated setting.

rows.strategy: Guarded read-mode agent, 12 changes per batch
rows.note: Four times the density: the single-step reading error at this density is about 6 per 100 changes, and it shows.

rows.strategy: Quoted events: the model quotes each change, code keeps the books, 480K narrative stream
rows.note: The model reports each change as one fixed-format line with an exact quote from the batch; the harness checks the quote is in the text, checks the counter and the amount, does the arithmetic itself, archives the batch and drops it. 479,512 tokens in 240 batches, 1.8 times the whole window: 578 calls, 573 with thinking off, 542 thinking tokens in the whole run. 23% faster than the read-mode agent on the same stream, and the arithmetic cannot go wrong. One seed.

rows.strategy: Quoted events, narrative text at 119K (3 changes per batch)
rows.note: After a bug in the harness's own number reader was fixed (it had refused correct lists and cost most of the time in the first runs). Faster than every other no-files strategy on this task and exact.

rows.strategy: Quoted events, retention test (two seeds)
rows.note: Seed 1 right on all but one. Seed 0 answered every current value but left the twelve old-value questions blank: the model compacted its own context and cut away the final batch that held the questions. Fixed by keeping that batch in the pinned message; rerun queued.

disk_estimate.status: Calculated payload and illustrative transfers; no completed disk-cache benchmark
disk_estimate.attention_payload_formula: 16 layers * 2 arrays * 4 KV heads * 256 head dimension * 2 bytes; target attention KV only, summed across both GPUs
disk_estimate.assumptions: One complete read of the attention cache at the stated hypothetical sustained storage bandwidth. Not an output-token rate. Excludes computation, recurrent/draft state, padding, metadata, and additional unoverlapped transfer. Partial residence, pipelining and speculative acceptance change the model calculation.
disk_estimate.streaming_status: Not implemented or benchmarked in the cited experiments

timing_analysis.method: Wall time and tool time from saved run records. Reading estimated from cold-read rates; writing is a residual and includes call overhead. Summary-call times are estimated. No per-token timestamps or isolated disk-I/O measurements.

cache_reuse.method: Common prefixes measured in rendered characters and converted to tokens with per-call ratios; not exact tokenization.

cache_break_even.method: Counterfactual calculation from saved calls and measured/assumed cold-read rates; not a paired cache-off run.

edit_cost.about: Wait before the first output token after one edit (a deletion) inside a cached prompt, exact prefix cache on. first_edit_s: first request after the edit; repeat_s: the same edited prompt sent again; cold_s: the same prompt with nothing cached. Fill a cell by setting status to "measured" and the three times, then run scripts/organize_results.py and scripts/build_site.py.
